topic.title: Cheaper to inject than to fix the canteen
topic.claim: We'd sooner buy a weekly injection than ask our office for a decent lunch.
topic.behaviour: Complaining about long hours and canteen food, then looking for a personal fix instead of a shared one.
topic.mechanism: Fixing a workplace needs a fight and an HR email. Fixing yourself is private, can be paid for and needs nobody's permission.
real_details: Researchers interviewed 79 urban adults aged 21 to 30 across eight metro cities
They found limited healthy food at workplaces and campuses is a major barrier to healthy living
Semaglutide's Indian patent expired on 20 March 2026
Generics launched at as little as ₹750 a week, or about ₹3,400 a month, though quoted prices vary widely by source
Insurance generally does not cover these drugs when used purely for obesity
topic.news_peg: Frontiers in Public Health study updated 13 October 2026, plus generic semaglutide launches since March 2026
topic.why_now: The study page was updated this month and generic GLP-1s are a hot topic in 30-something office circles.

score.reason: genuinely surprising, original pairing of two unrelated frustrations, anchored to current generic-GLP-1 news
score.best_hook: The canteen food hasn't changed in five years. But you'll happily pay twelve hundred rupees a week to inject your way around it.
